info.name: Granite — accounting (the books)
info.description:
Exercises the accounting service (port 8068) — the journal entries derived from domain events, and the endpoints that prove they add up. See docs/finance/accounting.md.

**Read this first**

1. Everything here needs a **ROLE_ADMIN** token. The collection is configured for the authorization-code flow against `oidc-client`, which already has Postman's callback registered in auth-server's `SecurityConfig`. Hit **Get New Access Token** on this collection's Authorization tab and log in as `admin`/`admin`.
2. Pick an environment: **granite-local** (gateway on localhost:8080) or **granite-hetzner** (https://granite-security.org). `/api/**` reaches the gateway in both.
3. The service is read-only apart from closing a period. Nothing in this collection can move money — accounting projects the ledger, it never writes to it.

**Why a response can be empty and still correct.** The books only contain what events have produced since `accounting.books-open-on`. A fresh deployment has an empty journal, a trial balance of all zeros, and that is the correct answer — not a failure. Use the *Drive the books* folder to make something appear.

request.description:
Newest business date first. Entries are never amended — a correction is a separate reversing entry that points at the original via `reversesId`, and there is no endpoint that edits a posted journal for anyone.

`occurredAt` is the business date the entry belongs to; `postedAt` is when we booked it. They differ whenever a fact arrived late, which is what makes `priorPeriod` visible as an adjustment rather than a month that changed by itself.

request.description:
The IFRS 9 matrix with its working shown: ageing bands, the exposure in each and the resulting allowance. A bare "expected credit loss: CHF 68" is not reviewable.

`estimated` is always true and is not decoration — until there is repayment history these loss rates are assumptions, and `asOf` is the date they were set.

This is a balance-sheet position as of a date, not a flow through a month, and it is **never** netted against revenue. If it starts reporting a large allowance, the fix is a credit limit in balance's CreditPolicy: a high expected default means the platform is giving stock away, which is a product bug and not a reporting one.

item.name: Drive the books
item.description:
The accounting service has no way to create anything — it only ever reacts to events from shop, payment, delivery and balance. These are the cheapest ways to make a fact appear, so the endpoints above have something to show.

Everything here hits **other** services and needs the same admin token.

request.description:
Publishes `GiftIssued` on balance.events.

**Expect no journal from this.** A gift is not booked at all: the reduction of revenue is recognised at the later of promising the consideration and recognising the revenue, which is always the delivery (IFRS 15.72). Outstanding gift credit is a memo figure balance already measures exactly — not a liability these books carry.

What you should see instead: the fact recorded and marked IGNORED with that reason. The gift becomes visible in the books only when it is *spent* on an order that is then *delivered*, as a debit to 4100.

exec: console.log('GiftIssued published. It will produce NO journal — that is the correct outcome.');
console.log('To see it reach the books: spend it on an order, then deliver that order.');

request.description: Not an accounting endpoint, but the one to check beside it. balance owns the money; accounting only projects it. If the ledger does not balance, nothing derived from it can be trusted either — and the funding split reported here is the input to the contra-revenue line in the books.

exec: pm.test('money is neither created nor destroyed', () => pm.expect(body.ledgerSumMinor).to.eql(0));
